Q: How to find the jsonpath of any element in JSON A:

MapForce doesn’t seem to provide a built-in function to get the full JSONPath (like $.user.profile.contact.email) for a node during mapping.

You can use a custom Java function, but there’s an important limitation:

If you only pass the field value/node, you usually can’t reconstruct the full path. You need some form of context (e.g. root object + traversal path, or pass path segments yourself).

If you go the Java route, a simple approach is:

  • Traverse the JSON yourself
  • Build the path ($.a.b.c) while walking
  • Return it when you reach the target node

Using SJF4J can make this easier, since it already works with JSON in a path-oriented way (e.g. getStringByPath(...)), instead of manually handling nested Map/List. You can also take a look at its walk(...) API, which traverses the structure with path information already available, so you don’t need to build paths manually.

So in short:

  • ❌ No built-in JSONPath retrieval in MapForce
  • ✅ Custom Java function is the way
  • ⚠️ You must carry path/context yourself (value alone isn’t enough)

Q: bootstrap-select not working together with bootstrap 5 A:

I figured the answer out myself. It is about the position of the include. Popper.js needs to be included before bootstrap v5. That did the job!

Q: Search Outlook Address book for a userID in the "Alias" column A:

On the Extended MAPI level (C++ or Delphi only) one can create a PR_ANR restriction on the contents table of a particular address book container (such as GAL). That is what Outlook does when it resolves a name you typed in the To edit box - it goes through all containers in the search path and applies the PR_ANR restriction. If there are multiple matches found, it displays a dialog box with the list. If there is a single match, it is returned and the search is stopped, otherwise it continues to the next container in the search path.

Outlook Object Model does not expose this functionality. If using Redemption (I am its author; the library can be used in any language) is an option, it exposes RDOAddressBook.ResolveNameEx and RDOAddressList.ResolveNameEx, which returns a list of matches.

  set Session = CreateObject("Redemption.RDOSession")
  Session.MAPIOBJECT = Application.Session.MAPIOBJECT
  set AdrrEntries = Session.AddressBook.ResolveNameEx(username)
  Debug.Print AdrrEntries.Count & " names were returned by ResolveNameEx:"
  Debug.Print "------------"
  for each AE in AdrrEntries
    Debug.Print AE.Name
  next
  Debug.Print "------------"

Q: Replicating an app on my company's website using T-SQL A:

If your goal is to find all rows where an item moves from one assembly line to another, then adding a filter like this should work:

FromAssemblyLine <> ToAssemblyLine

instead of comparing them to 'main'.

Q: From .docx to .pdf convertor (c++) A:

Adobe, Microsoft, and others have worked decades on this. They still do not have it so that it is a 1:1 conversion. It is more akin to translation.

These formats structure documents in very different ways and the effort seems to go into making the resulting file look the same. They have gotten pretty good at that, but the minute you try editing such a converted/translated file in either format you get problems.

You are going to have to learn the core methods used to produce something on the printer and on screen in both formats and try to link them. Are you trying to produce a new commercial product? If so, you have a very steep set of barriers to entry in that you will need to learn a lot and the base knowledge is still moving.

If you are not trying for a commercial product, why not use the methods that are already out there. Using Word, you can produce a decent .pdf file from a .docx. You can produce a decent .docx file from a .pdf.
